findings.title: Recreate exit code silently changed from 4 to 3 and 4 reused for a different meaning
findings.body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` is changed from `4` to `3`, and `4` is now reused for the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` result. Any existing consumer (user automation/CI pipelines built on the documented exit code, and the Keycloak Operator logic that inspects the exit code of the `update-compatibility check` run) that interprets `4` as "recreate upgrade required" will now interpret a *feature-disabled* failure as a recreate decision, and will no longer recognize a real recreate decision (`3`). This PR contains no corresponding change on the Operator/consumer side, so if the Operator hardcodes the old value the update strategy decision becomes wrong. At minimum the renumbering should be called out as a breaking change, and the Operator path that reads this code has to be verified/updated.

findings.title: New feature-gate exit code and the renumbered recreate exit code are not asserted
findings.body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error text and never asserts `exitCode() == 4` (`CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED`). There is also no test for `update-compatibility check` with the feature disabled, and no test asserts the new recreate exit code `3` (the `testWrongVersions` test only checks the printed message). Since the exit codes are the documented, script-facing contract of these commands (and were just renumbered in this PR), a regression in any of them would go undetected.

findings.title: Test overwrites any pre-existing enabled features and only enables the flag for non-default strategies
findings.body: `setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))` replaces the whole enabled-features list rather than appending, so if `getTestKeycloakDeployment()` ever sets features in the spec they are silently dropped (the preceding `getFeatureSpec() == null` guard suggests the intent was to preserve existing content). Additionally the feature is only enabled when `updateStrategy != null`, so the default (unset) strategy path runs without the `rolling-updates` feature; if the Operator is supposed to require the feature for the update logic (as the new operator docs claim), that path is untested, and if it is not required, the docs are wrong.

findings.title: CAUTION overstates that rolling-updates must be enabled for all update strategies
findings.body: The new CAUTION block states that while in preview the `rolling-updates` feature "must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail", but the NOTE immediately below describes the default (strategy not set) behaviour which mimics Keycloak 26.1 and does not require the feature — and the operator test only enables the feature for the non-default strategies. As written, users are told to enable a preview feature even when they are relying on the default behaviour. The caution should be scoped to the cases where the feature is actually required (i.e. when `spec.update.strategy` is used).

findings.title: Exit code 4 description is misleading
findings.body: Exit code 4 is documented as "Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled." In reality the command refuses to run at all and produces no compatibility verdict (see `printFeatureDisabled()`/`FEATURE_DISABLED`): no metadata is written and no comparison happens. Describing it as a rolling-upgrade verdict can lead script authors to treat it as a valid "recreate required" answer instead of a configuration error that must be fixed.
